xmldoc.short_description: Load and save parts of variables in a MAT-file.

param_input_item.param_description: character vector or string scalar: MAT-file name. Without extension, .mat is appended. A relative name is searched in the current folder, then on the search path.
logical scalar: enables or disables saving through the object. Default is false for an existing file and true for a new file.
one subscript per dimension: a positive integer, an increasing range with a constant step such as 10:2:50, or :.
variable names, with the * wildcard, or '-regexp' followed by regular expressions.

param_output_item.param_description: nelson.io.MatFile handle object connected to the file.

description.p: matfile creates an object connected to a MAT-file. No data is read when the object is created. Variables of the file are accessed with the dot syntax, as fields of a structure.

m.name loads the whole variable. m.name(i1, ..., iN) loads only the selected block. On Version 7.3 MAT-files, numeric and logical variables are read directly from the file, so a block of a large variable is read without loading the variable. Other classes, and files of older versions, load the whole variable before indexing it; older versions also emit the warning Nelson:matfile:wholeVariableLoad.

m.name = value adds or replaces a variable. m.name(i1, ..., iN) = value changes a block. On Version 7.3 MAT-files, a block inside a numeric, char or logical variable is written in place. A block outside the current size grows the variable, filled with zeros. A new variable is created with the class of the assigned value. m.name(i1, ..., iN) = [] deletes the selected elements.
When the file does not exist, it is created as a Version 7.3 MAT-file on the first assignment.
The object has one property, Properties, with two fields:

ul.li: Properties.Source: full path of the MAT-file (read-only).
Properties.Writable: logical scalar, whether assignments are allowed.
Give a subscript for every dimension: linear indexing is not supported.
Only () indexing is supported, with numeric subscripts. Ranges must increase with a constant step.
Using end in a subscript loads the whole variable. Use size(m, name) to get the size without loading data.

The assigned value must have the class of the variable, or another floating-point class for a floating-point variable, or another integer class for an integer variable. A complex value cannot be assigned into a real variable.
A block of a sparse variable can be read but not assigned.
String arrays, function handles and objects can be loaded or saved as a whole only.

description.p: size, who and whos inspect the file without loading the variables. Call them with function syntax, for example size(m, 'x').

example_item.example_item_description: Save blocks of a variable, then load a part of it.
Mean of each column without loading the whole variable.
Enable write access to an existing file.
